newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods soften as buying evaporates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods soften as buying evaporates.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices softened Wednesday as traders waited for Wednesday's inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API), brokerage sources said.
The report, due out later today, is being released a day late because of the U.S. Presidents' Day holiday on Monday.
Spot buyers stayed on the sidelines to assess how much higher NYMEX would climb following a volatile session yesterday.
"It's dead. There's been no bids for three days," a broker said.
Offers for conventional unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles were 68 cents a gallon, off one cent from Tuesday. Sellers priced CARB-grade gasoline a cent lower at 74 cents.
Bay area gasoline stood around three cents a gallon lower than L.A. material.
Distillates also retreated, with low sulphur diesel offers falling a cent to 71 cents.
